steps.title: 01-open: Open http://127.0.0.1:3000/. If the Grafana sign-in page appears, sign in with username admin and password {{env:APP_PASSWORD}} (type the password text exactly as {{env:APP_PASSWORD}}). Then open the provisioned dashboard named 'Service health' - find it via search or the Dashboards browse page - and report the titles of all the panels on that dashboard, exactly as they are displayed on the page.

02-create: Create a NEW Grafana dashboard (Dashboards > New dashboard, or the + Create > Dashboard menu). Add a panel of visualization type 'Stat' (not timeseries). Set the panel's title to exactly '{{runid}} Availability'. Set its data source to the 'TestData' data source (in the query editor, pick TestData from the data source selector; the default TestData query scenario is fine). Then save the dashboard with the title exactly '{{runid}} Bench Dashboard' (Save dashboard dialog: name it that, leave folder as General unless it insists otherwise, and click Save). After saving, report the dashboard's URL as shown in the browser address bar and confirm the Stat panel titled '{{runid}} Availability' is visible on the saved dashboard.

03-edit: On the Grafana dashboard at http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/{{02-create.url.p1}}/{{runid}}-bench-dashboard (titled '{{runid}} Bench Dashboard'), enter edit mode (Edit button / pencil icon) and add a NEW panel of visualization type 'Text'. Set that Text panel's title to exactly '{{runid}} Notes', and set its text content to include the runid - e.g. content like 'Bench notes for run {{runid}}' (the content must contain the string {{runid}}). Then save the dashboard (click Save in the top bar; if a save dialog appears, keep the existing name '{{runid}} Bench Dashboard' and click Save). After saving, verify in view mode that both panels are present: the Stat panel '{{runid}} Availability' and the Text panel '{{runid}} Notes' with content containing {{runid}}. Report what you see.

04-edit: On the Grafana dashboard '{{runid}} Bench Dashboard' (http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/{{02-create.url.p1}}/{{runid}}-bench-dashboard), first exit panel edit mode if it is still active (click Back or Discard if prompted, so you are in normal view mode). Then do two things and save: (1) Open the dashboard settings (gear icon) and add the tag 'bench' to the dashboard's tags (Dashboard settings > General > Tags, type bench and add it), then Save settings. (2) Set the dashboard time range to 'Last 6 hours' using the top-bar time picker, then click Save dashboard in the top bar and in the save dialog TICK the checkbox 'Update default time range' before clicking Save, so the 6-hour range is persisted into the saved dashboard. Handle any version-conflict prompt with 'Save and overwrite'. Finally verify: reopen the dashboard fresh (reload the page / navigate to the dashboard URL again) and confirm the tag 'bench' appears on the dashboard (e.g. in the header or via settings) and the saved default time range is Last 6 hours. Report what you observed.

05-set: On the Grafana dashboard '{{runid}} Bench Dashboard' (http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/{{02-create.url.p1}}/{{runid}}-bench-dashboard), set the dashboard's auto-refresh interval to '1m': use the top-bar refresh-interval picker (the clock/refresh dropdown next to the time range picker, often under a 'Refresh' heading) and select '1m' (1 minute). Then click Save dashboard in the top bar; in the save dialog, if there is a checkbox 'Update default time range', tick it, then click Save (handle any version-conflict prompt with 'Save and overwrite'). Then VERIFY persistence by opening Dashboard settings (gear icon) > JSON model (or 'JSON Model' tab) and reading the saved JSON: report the exact values of the top-level "refresh" field, the top-level "time" object (from/to), and the "tags" array. Also report the dashboard UID from the JSON. If the refresh field is not "1m" in the saved JSON, retry setting it and saving until it is.

06-report: Navigate to the Grafana dashboard '{{runid}} Bench Dashboard' by opening a fresh URL with NO query parameters: http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/{{02-create.url.p1}}/{{runid}}-bench-dashboard (make sure the address bar has no ?from=...&refresh=... etc. - if parameters get appended, clear them and reload). Once it loads in normal view mode, report: (1) the exact URL currently shown in the browser address bar, (2) the titles of all panels visible on the dashboard, (3) what the top-bar time range picker shows, (4) what the top-bar auto-refresh interval picker shows, and (5) whether the tag 'bench' is listed in Dashboard settings > General > Tags.
